title: Do it again
summary: Automate repeated work with a loop and check the number of repetitions.

scenario.briefing: Five parcels wait at the packing line. The robot arm repeats one labeled cycle for every parcel. A wrong count leaves a parcel unpacked or runs an extra cycle.

objectives.description: Choose the correct number of repetitions.
Order the actions inside the repeated block.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Count the parcels that need packing.
Each cycle should label, seal, and scan one parcel.
Five parcels means five cycles. Inside a cycle, the label goes on before sealing.
Repeat 5 times. Each cycle: apply label, seal the box, scan the label.

misconceptions.description: One repetition short because counting starts at zero.
misconceptions.feedback: There are five parcels. The loop must run five times. Starting an index at zero does not reduce the number of parcels.
The scanner reads the label, so the label must be attached before sealing and scanning. Order matters inside the loop body.

sections.title: Loops repeat a block
sections.body: A loop runs the same block of steps more than once. The loop needs a stopping rule, such as a fixed count or a condition that becomes false. The block should leave the system in a valid state after each pass.

sections.title: Counts and boundaries
sections.body: Repeating five times means exactly five passes. An off-by-one error produces four or six. When you write loops later, test the first and last iteration because those boundaries reveal counting mistakes.

vocabulary.definition: One pass through a loop body.
The steps repeated on each pass.

steps.title: Program the packing cycle
steps.prompt: Choose the repetition count and arrange the block. The robot runs the block once per pass.
steps.explanation: Five parcels need five cycles. Each cycle labels, seals, and then scans one parcel.

steps.title: Trace two passes
steps.prompt: Follow the loop for two iterations. Then enter the final values of packed and boxesLeft.

snapshots.note: After two passes, two boxes are packed.

steps.explanation: Each pass adds one to packed and subtracts one from boxesLeft. Two passes produce packed 2 and boxesLeft 3.

steps.title: A different repetition
steps.prompt: A water tank starts with 40 liters. A pump adds 5 liters per minute for 6 minutes. Which loop describes the process?

options.label: Add 30 liters once, without a loop

quiz.explanation: Six minutes at five liters per minute means six repetitions of add five liters. A single addition could produce the same total but no longer describes the timed process.

hints: How much is added per minute?

accessibility.summary: The repetition count is a group of buttons and the body order uses move buttons. The trace exposes each watched value as text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Choose a repetition count with arrow keys or buttons. Move body actions with the up and down buttons.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The loop is announced as a block that repeats the selected number of times. Each trace step announces the line and updated values.
